question: How does the common-substratum thought reveal the Sadāśiva-state?
premises: Having seen knower-ness with heart-throbbing vision, difference concealed in own consciousness within the clear object.
Since he fully sees, thereby may the common-substratum thought, attaining I-knower unity-difference, reveal the Sadāśiva-state.
inference: Full seeing of concealed difference yields the common-substratum thought revealing Sadāśiva-state.
plain_english: Having seen knower-ness with the eye throbbing in the hearts interior — in the clearly shining object the concealment of difference in own consciousness — since he fully sees, thereby may the thought of common-substratum-ness, swiftly attaining the unity-and-difference of I and knower, reveal the Sadāśiva-state.
